steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch pie plate.
Place milk, coconut, eggs, butter, sugar, flour, and vanilla in a blender; blend until well mixed. Pour into prepared pie plate. Sprinkle nutmeg on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Impossibly Easy Coconut Pie
raw_recipe.description: This impossible coconut pie recipe blends and bakes milk, eggs, flaked coconut, and a few other easy ingredients into amazing coconut custard pie.
raw_recipe.name: Impossibly Easy Coconut Pie

review.reviewBody: I read all reviews before I decided to make this. It was simple, quick (you just stick everything in a blender), and really good. I added 14 oz. of coconut as that's what my frozen bag was and I read how people were adding more and figured why not, and 3 jumbo eggs. I baked it an hour. My husband liked it warm and it's good warm/cold, but if you want the firmer texture you need to leave it in the fridge. The only reason I can think of for any negative review of this recipe is people making the wrong recipe. If you want to invest a mere several minutes prep time, you should make this - it's excellent for what it is! - but if you want minimal work yet are expecting the outcome of a gourmet coconut pie you'd find in a restaurant.. it's common sense. I noticed one reviewer said it "doesn't make its own crust." Again - if you are expecting to open the oven door and suddenly see a dough crust magically formed around the pie, you shouldn't be making this recipe. But if you're cool with a "crust" (a.k.a. firm, golden texture all around the pie that makes it totally non-stick and easy to lift out - I used a clear glass pie dish so I could see what the outside was doing, and when I ate it the edges were chewy) then this recipe is for you. The only thing I would add next time is a little salt, I think it will accent the flavor. Hope this is helpful to someone. :)

I was craving coconut pie and had all the ingredients but did want to go through the time of making the crust. This hit the spot! I also made some suggested changes using more coconut and sprinkling some on top before baking, using 3 eggs instead of 4 and using coconut extract instead of vanilla. I also used butter instead of margarine. It was scrumptious warm while the top was crunchy and toasty!

This is similar to a recipe that I have made for years. I was craving it and found this updated recipe. It is a winner. I did make some changes because my pie plates went missing (aka son and daughter went shopping in my cabinet). I made it in a deep dish small Pyrex casserole dish, which turned out perfectly because it has a lid to it. Using the casserole dish with cover makes it easy to transport if taking somewhere. I decreased the egg to 3 because my eggs were jumbo. Instead of using vanilla, I used a combination of rum and coconut flavoring. Mixing it up in a blender is a great idea. I used my Ninja and it mixed perfectly. Next time I may add a little bit more flour, but it really isn't necessary. I did add additional coconut, and I think it made it a pretty brown. I baked for 1hour and allowed to cool. Cooling is essential because it is VERY hot and you can burn your mouth terribly if you give in to temptation. It also allows for the pie to set up better.

I would give it a 5 for easiness & taste. I doubled the ingredients so 2 (2 cups coconut milk, 2 eggs and 2 yolks, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 a bag of shredded coconut (about 2 1/4 cup unpressed), 1tsp vanilla, 5 TBs butter, 1/2 C sugar & 1/2 cup flour). I got rid of my blender so I stuffed what I could in my nutri bullet blended then poured into a bowl then mixed the remaining ingredients poured into bowl quick mix then poured into a 9 " rectangular glass pan and bake at 350 for 1 hour..
Cooled overnight then toasted remain coconut in the broiler and added raspberries before taking to church luncheon for dessert. It was a great hit and everyone wanted the recipe that I remembered because it was so easy.

The original recipe I used for this pie required 8 TBLs of butter (1 stick) and not margarine. That was WAYYYYY too much and made it pour grease and stay liquified. I would suggest 1/2 stick ( 4 TBLs.) None of the recipes tell you whether to use cold, room temp or melted butter - use melted or almost melted. (Tried cold the first time and it will ruin it). I would reduce eggs to no more than 3 as it does have an eggy texture as the eggs are cooking in the butter part inside. Cook time is at least an hour and it puffs up pretty high in the middle when it is close to ready, this falls once it starts cooling down. Before putting it in the oven, I let it rest 5 mins so heavier ingredients settle to the bottom for the crust and then sprinkle fresh nutmeg all over the top. Delicious and sweet pie, love the brown crust on top the best, easy! Oh, I also add extra coconut (about an extra half cup) and 1.5 tsp of vanilla. Enjoy! Details matter. I also did mine in a bowl with an electric blender. It is very soupy and the first time it splattered on my wall! I am a seasoned cook, so I knew better but thought it would thicken (it doesn't). Very full pie plate, use foil on the rack below to catch overflow.

I’ve been looking for a custard coconut pie, but most of the recipes have 2+ cups of sugar. This was just about right. I reduced the sugar to 2/3 cup, my coconut was unsweetened btw, and I used 1 cup half & half, and 1 cup water. 
I omitted the flour, here’s why:
I love piecrust! Absolutely love it. So I put this custard into a uncooked piecrust. This is a traditional pie crust made from lard. Baked at 400° for 40 minutes. 
Perfection!

Have been making this for years. Sometimes I use chocolate silk instead of milk. Tonight my 7 year old grand daughter and I made individual pies in a 6 pie pan we used 1 cup almond milk 1 cup coconut milk,1/4 cup sugar and 8 packs of sweetleaf stevia, also we sparkled chopped on almonds on top and baked for 12 minutes...Awesome!

I used a blend of almond and coconut milk, used 2 cups of coconut and poured it into two smaller pans so 45 minutes was just right. Delicious. Friends liked it and wanted the recipe. My dog could smell it and wanted some also. :)

Made it twice in a week for two different events, both times it was a HIT! I followed other reviews by using only 3 large eggs, I replaced milk with coconut milk, and only added 1/2 cup of sugar. I used 1 cup of dried coconut flakes in the mixture and sprinkled an additional 1/2 cup on top. Baked for 45 minutes and the top is nice and golden and crunchy!

This pie was great and exceptionally easy to make. Most people have these ingredients in their house so that makes it even better. If you have coconut extract use that instead of the vanilla extract. If not, no biggie. I used only 3 eggs and baked it for 60 minutes as the other reviews suggested. It came out perfectly! Also- I didn't have a pie plate, so I baked it in a cake pan and it came out fine. Yum!
You don't need the blender. Just a good whisk and it turns out fine.
This is so good. I didn't blend mine. I double the recipe for a family event. Glad I did.
I make this pie all the time, and it's delicious! It's a comfort food, for sure. I never change a thing! Though, I may switch out one cup milk with one cup canned coconut milk, someday :)

Loved this! This is so easy and so good with no changes. I made it exactly as stated in the recipe with 45 minutes in the oven and it turned out wonderfully! There was a small crust layer on bottom, a nice custard in the middle and a buttery, flakey coconut layer on top. Thanks for the recipe!
I made this and it turned out beautifully. Simply love it

Great, used medium eggs as that's all I had and a cup and a half of fresh grated coconut. Took longer to cook about 20 minutes on gas 4 but that could be my oven, it's not as good as the last one I had. Left in the tin to cool and ate some warm. Like an egg custard with coconut in it. Love that it can be made without pasty.
Super easy recipe 9:30 at night my home smelled of vanilla and butter I couldn’t wait to taste I used 3 eggs and topped with coconut beforehand Baked 1 hour 5 minutes..
Simple and delicious. We were very pleased with the result. It's like an eggy coconut custard pie with only a fraction of the effort.
I made this for husband for Valentines Day. It’s a surprise. It turned it quite well. Really easy to make.
